q1: SELECT EMAIL AS EMAIL FROM PERSON GROUP BY EMAIL HAVING COUNT(EMAIL) >1
q2: SELECT EMAIL AS EMAIL FROM PERSON GROUP BY 1 HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT ID) >1
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT EMAIL AS EMAIL FROM PERSON GROUP BY EMAIL HAVING COUNT(EMAIL) >1
q2_prompt_sql: SELECT EMAIL AS EMAIL FROM PERSON GROUP BY 1 HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT ID) >1
explanation: Q1 groups by EMAIL and counts the number of occurrences of each email. It returns emails that appear more than once. Q2 groups by the first column (EMAIL) and counts distinct IDs for each email group. The COUNT(DISTINCT ID) > 1 condition ensures that each email has more than one distinct person associated with it. These are not equivalent because Q1 counts rows per email (including duplicates of the same person), while Q2 counts distinct persons per email.
counterexample_dsp: A test case with one email appearing twice for the same person (ID) and one email appearing once for a different person. Q1 will return the email with two rows (same person), while Q2 will not return that email since COUNT(DISTINCT ID) = 1.
